# OPEN BLOCKERS — ARKALI GENESIS v2

**As of:** Phase 0 candidate

## Internal blockers

**Status is declared, never inferred.** Each finding's state comes only from its
`Status` cell. Free text in any other column may contain OPEN, CLOSED, HIGH,
`ark_req_ids_closed` or any other token without effect (F-0025).

| F-0036 | **A durability predicate was named for the heartbeat and measured the deadline.** Package 2 shipped `JobExecution.heartbeat_expired`, which resolved through `_expired` to `clock >= attempt.deadline_at` and **never read `heartbeat_at` at all** — proven by AST before anything was edited: the function's attribute reads were `{_clock, deadline_at}`, and the only reader of `heartbeat_at` in the module was the writer that sets it. The name promised *silence since the last proof of life*; the behaviour measured *elapsed work*. The two are independent — a worker that heartbeated this instant is past its deadline eventually, and a worker silent for a week is not — so the function was a correct `timed_out` under a name that described a different fact. Package 2 was unaffected because both of its callers meant timeout and `timed_out` merely delegated to it. It would have become a real defect at the moment of consumption: `EXECUTION_AND_CAPABILITY.md` §3 keys crash recovery on a job "without a live heartbeat", so Package 3 reading the existing name would have recovered live workers past their deadline and left genuinely dead ones holding their jobs for the whole timeout. Both directions are also proven behaviourally: a silent execution is recovered long before its deadline, and one reporting normally past its deadline is not stale. The old name is banned by a negative control |
